items.claim: `HTTPBasicAuth` inherits from `AuthBase`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `class HTTPBasicAuth(AuthBase)` is declared directly as a subclass of `AuthBase`.

items.claim: When a redirect changes the method from POST/PUT/PATCH to GET, `resolve_redirects` removes the Content-Length, Content-Type, and Transfer-Encoding headers.
items.label: supported
items.reason: For redirect statuses other than 307/308 (i.e. the cases where the method is downgraded to GET), `resolve_redirects` pops Content-Length, Content-Type and Transfer-Encoding and clears the body.

items.claim: If an integer `max_retries` is passed to `HTTPAdapter`, `Retry.from_int` builds the retry policy.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The constructor calls `Retry.from_int(max_retries)` for an int argument (except the default 0, which short-circuits to `Retry(0, read=False)`).

items.claim: For redirect statuses other than 307 and 308, `resolve_redirects` discards the body and the `Content-Length`, `Content-Type` and `Transfer-Encoding` headers.
items.label: supported
items.reason: For responses not 307/308, the purged_headers tuple (Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding) is popped and body is set to None.

items.claim: `Session.should_strip_auth` strips auth on any hostname change, permits an `http`→`https` upgrade on standard ports, permits a same-scheme hop between default ports, and otherwise strips on a changed port or scheme.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The method returns True on hostname change, False for http→https on standard ports, False for unchanged scheme with default ports, otherwise `changed_port or changed_scheme`.

items.claim: In the stream branch of `prepare_body`, `self._body_position = body.tell()` is recorded, and if `tell()` raises `OSError` a bare `object()` sentinel is stored instead.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The stream branch records `self._body_position = body.tell()` and stores `object()` when `tell()` raises OSError.

items.claim: `_parse_content_type_header` strips quotes and whitespace from parameter values.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `strip_chars = "\"' "` is applied to both key and value of each parameter, stripping quotes and whitespace.

items.claim: Requests v2.34.2 moved `headers` types back to `Mapping` from `MutableMapping`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The repo shows version 2.34.2 and Mapping-typed headers, but the changelog entry attributing this change to that release is in HISTORY.md, which is not shown.

items.claim: A minor release of Requests uses version format vX.Y.0 and includes new features and bug fixes that are backwards compatible.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The release process doc states minor releases are versioned vX.Y.0, contain no breaking changes, and remain backwards compatible within the major version.

items.claim: `Session.get_adapter` raises `InvalidSchema(f"No connection adapters were found for {url!r}")` when no mounted prefix matches.
items.label: supported
items.reason: get_adapter raises exactly `InvalidSchema(f"No connection adapters were found for {url!r}")` when no prefix matches.

items.claim: In `Session.request`, a URL passed as `bytes` is decoded as UTF-8.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Session.request decodes a bytes url with `url.decode("utf-8")`.

items.claim: `Response.ok` is True if `status_code` is between 200 and 299.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: `ok` returns True whenever `raise_for_status()` doesn't raise, i.e. for any status code below 400 (including 3xx), not only 200-299.

items.claim: `TooManyRedirects` is raised when the request exceeds the configured number of maximum redirects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `resolve_redirects` raises `TooManyRedirects` once `len(resp.history) >= self.max_redirects`.

items.claim: `prepare_auth` does not check the URL scheme before attaching Basic credentials.
items.label: supported
items.reason: prepare_auth inspects only the auth value/URL credentials; there is no scheme check before applying HTTPBasicAuth.

items.claim: `Session.request` builds a `Request` passing `data=data or {}` and `params=params or {}`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The Request is constructed with `data=data or {}` and `params=params or {}`.

items.claim: The tox `use_chardet_on_py3` environment tests with the `chardet` extra enabled.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: tox.ini is not among the displayed files, so its environments cannot be checked.

items.claim: `Response.apparent_encoding` uses charset_normalizer or chardet to guess the encoding.
items.label: supported
items.reason: apparent_encoding calls `chardet.detect`, where `chardet` is resolved from chardet or charset_normalizer, falling back to 'utf-8'.

items.claim: `Session.get` sets `allow_redirects` to `True` by default.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Session.get does `kwargs.setdefault("allow_redirects", True)`.

items.claim: The Sphinx `source_suffix` is `".rst"`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `source_suffix = ".rst"` is set in the Sphinx config.

items.claim: `bool(r)` on a `Response` is equivalent to `status_code < 400`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__bool__` returns `self.ok`, which is False only when raise_for_status raises for 4xx/5xx, i.e. effectively status_code < 400.

items.claim: `MockRequest` wraps a `PreparedRequest` and exposes `get_type()`, `get_host()` and `get_full_url()` by re-parsing `self._r.url`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: MockRequest wraps a PreparedRequest and derives type/host/full URL from `urlparse(self._r.url)` (the scheme being cached at init).

items.claim: `get_encoding_from_headers` returns `ISO-8859-1` for a content type containing `text` when no charset is given.
items.label: supported
items.reason: get_encoding_from_headers returns "ISO-8859-1" when no charset param and 'text' appears in the content type.

items.claim: `guess_json_utf` examines the first 4 bytes of the data.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The function takes `sample = data[:4]` and bases BOM/null-count detection on those first four bytes.

items.claim: `Response.iter_content` raises `TypeError` for a non-integer chunk size.
items.label: supported
items.reason: iter_content raises TypeError when chunk_size is not None and not an int.

items.claim: When `auth` is `None`, `prepare_auth` calls `get_auth_from_url(self.url)` and uses any `user:pass@` embedded in the URL as credentials.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When auth is None, prepare_auth extracts credentials from the URL via get_auth_from_url and uses them if any are present.

items.claim: Immediately after `rebuild_auth` strips credentials, `.netrc` may supply fresh credentials for the new host if `trust_env` is enabled.
items.label: supported
items.reason: After deleting the Authorization header, rebuild_auth consults get_netrc_auth(url) when trust_env is True and re-applies it.

items.claim: When sending a request, the session selects the adapter with the longest matching prefix for the target URL.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `mount` keeps adapters ordered by descending prefix length and `get_adapter` returns the first prefix match, yielding longest-prefix selection.

items.claim: `Response.text` accesses `self.content` twice: once for an emptiness check and once to decode.
items.label: supported
items.reason: text checks `if not self.content: return ""` and later decodes `self.content`, accessing the property twice.

items.claim: `Session.__enter__` returns the session itself.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__enter__` returns self.

items.claim: The hook system is defined in `src/requests/hooks.py`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: HOOKS, default_hooks and dispatch_hook implementing the hook system live in src/requests/hooks.py.

items.claim: `Response.__repr__` renders a response as `<Response [200]>` for status 200.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__repr__` formats as `<Response [{status_code}]>`.

items.claim: `requests.utils.guess_filename(obj)` guesses the filename of a file-like object by checking the `name` attribute.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `guess_filename` reads `getattr(obj, "name", None)` and returns its basename.

items.claim: All Requests exceptions inherit from `RequestException`, which inherits from `IOError`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `RequestException(IOError)` is the base and every error class in exceptions.py derives from it.

items.claim: `Request.__init__` converts `hooks=None` into `{}`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Request.__init__ sets `hooks = {} if hooks is None else hooks`.

items.claim: `should_bypass_proxies` calls `proxy_bypass(hostname)` inside a `with set_environ("no_proxy", no_proxy_arg)` block.
items.label: supported
items.reason: should_bypass_proxies wraps the proxy_bypass(hostname) call in `with set_environ("no_proxy", no_proxy_arg)`.

items.claim: `InvalidURL` is raised for malformed URLs.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `InvalidURL` is defined and raised by `prepare_url` for unparsable/invalid-label URLs.

items.claim: `LookupDict.__getattr__` looks up keys in `__dict__` and raises AttributeError if missing.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `__getattr__` returns `self.__dict__[key]` when present and otherwise raises AttributeError.

items.claim: The `Session` class maintains state across multiple requests, including cookies and connection pooling.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The Session docstring and __init__ show cookie persistence and mounted HTTPAdapters providing connection pooling across requests.

items.claim: `Response.iter_content` returns the `generate()` generator without starting it when the response has not been consumed.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When `_content_consumed` is False, `chunks = generate()` creates the generator which is returned un-iterated (unless decode_unicode wraps it).

items.claim: The `CaseInsensitiveDict` docstring states that if two keys differ only in case, the behavior is undefined.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The docstring states that keys with equal `.lower()`s given to the constructor, update, or equality comparison produce undefined behavior.

items.claim: During preparation, auth is applied after headers, so netrc credentials take precedence over an `Authorization` header set via `headers=`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: prepare_headers runs before prepare_auth, and the netrc-derived HTTPBasicAuth overwrites headers["Authorization"] last.

items.claim: The `Response` object contains the original `PreparedRequest` in its `request` attribute.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Response.request` is typed as PreparedRequest and set to the sent request in `build_response`.

items.claim: The `Session` automatically extracts cookies from responses and includes them in subsequent requests using a `RequestsCookieJar`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Session cookies are a RequestsCookieJar populated via `extract_cookies_to_jar` on send and merged into each prepared request.

items.claim: The Requests version is dynamically pulled from `requests.__version__.__version__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The version string is defined in requests/__version__.py, re-exported in the package, and read dynamically (e.g. by docs/conf.py).

items.claim: If a single callable is provided as a hook, `dispatch_hook` wraps it in a list before execution.
items.label: supported
items.reason: dispatch_hook checks `isinstance(hook_list, Callable)` and wraps it in a list before iterating.

items.claim: `_parse_content_type_header` converts parameter names to lowercase.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The parameter key is stored with `params_dict[key.lower()] = value`.

items.claim: A major release of Requests uses version format vX.0.0 and includes breaking changes.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The release process doc states major releases include breaking changes and are versioned vX.0.0.

items.claim: `setup.py` checks `sys.version_info` and exits with an error if the Python version is below 3.10.
items.label: supported
items.reason: setup.py checks `sys.version_info < (3, 10)` and exits with an error message.

items.claim: `HTTPAdapter` implements `BaseAdapter`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: HTTPAdapter is declared as a subclass of BaseAdapter.

items.claim: `Session.prepare_request` upper-cases the method at sessions.py line 542.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Line 542 inside prepare_request passes `method=method.upper()` to p.prepare().

items.claim: `_parse_content_type_header` sets the value to `True` for parameters without values.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: The loop only records parameters containing '=', and never assigns True for value-less parameters.

items.claim: In `_urllib3_request_context`, if `client_cert` is not a 2-tuple, the value is assigned to `cert_file`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When client_cert is not a 2-tuple, the else branch sets `pool_kwargs["cert_file"] = client_cert`.

items.claim: The Sphinx `templates_path` is set to `["_templates"]`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: conf.py sets `templates_path = ["_templates"]`.

items.claim: `HTTPAdapter.close` clears its PoolManager and any ProxyManagers, closing the pooled connections.
items.label: supported
items.reason: close() calls self.poolmanager.clear() and clears each proxy manager, as documented in its docstring.

items.claim: `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout` is raised when the server does not send data within the read timeout period.
items.label: supported
items.reason: ReadTimeout is documented as 'The server did not send any data in the allotted amount of time' and is raised from urllib3's ReadTimeoutError.

items.claim: `Session.__init__` sets `self.cert = None`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Session.__init__ assigns self.cert = None.

items.claim: Requests uses `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` as a fallback if `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` is not set.
items.label: supported
items.reason: merge_environment_settings falls back to CURL_CA_BUNDLE when REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE is unset.

items.claim: `make test-readme` uses `setup.py check` to validate RestructuredText for PyPI.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The Makefile contents were not shown, so the test-readme target cannot be checked.

items.claim: `MockRequest.get_full_url()` prefers a caller-set `Host` header over the URL's host when determining the request's domain.
items.label: supported
items.reason: get_full_url returns the plain URL only when no Host header is set; otherwise it rebuilds the URL using the Host header value.

items.claim: `Session.prepare_request` never mutates `session.cookies`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The session jar is only used as the source argument to merge_cookies into a fresh RequestsCookieJar, which copies cookies rather than mutating the session jar.

items.claim: `HTTPDigestAuth` supports both `str` and `bytes` for credentials.
items.label: supported
items.reason: HTTPDigestAuth declares username/password as `bytes | str` with overloads for both str and bytes.

items.claim: `HTTPAdapter.send` calls `conn.urlopen` with `redirect=False`, `assert_same_host=False`, `preload_content=False`, `decode_content=False`, `retries=self.max_retries`, and the resolved timeout and chunked flag.
items.label: supported
items.reason: conn.urlopen is invoked with exactly those keyword arguments including redirect=False, preload_content=False, decode_content=False, retries=self.max_retries, timeout=resolved_timeout and chunked=chunked.

items.claim: `Session.get_redirect_target` consults `resp.is_redirect`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: get_redirect_target branches on `if resp.is_redirect:` before returning the location.

items.claim: If `idna` lacks a `__version__` attribute, Requests returns an empty string rather than crashing.
items.label: supported
items.reason: idna version is obtained via `getattr(idna, "__version__", "")`, defaulting to an empty string.

items.claim: Comments in `PreparedRequest.prepare` state that `prepare_hooks` must come after `prepare_auth` because an auth handler may register a hook.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The comments state prepare_auth must be last and that prepare_hooks must go after it because authenticators could add a hook.

items.claim: After calling the auth handler, `prepare_auth` runs `self.__dict__.update(r.__dict__)` and then `self.prepare_content_length(self.body)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: After calling auth_handler, the code updates __dict__ from the returned request and then calls prepare_content_length(self.body).

items.claim: Python 3.14 support was added in Requests v2.32.5.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: HISTORY.md was not shown, so the release note about Python 3.14 in v2.32.5 cannot be verified.

items.claim: Ruff is configured to use double quotes and space indentation.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: pyproject.toml contents were not shown, so Ruff formatting configuration cannot be checked.

items.claim: `HTTPBasicAuth.__call__` mutates the request in place and returns the same object.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __call__ sets r.headers["Authorization"] on the passed request and returns r itself.

items.claim: `resolve_redirects` accepts a `yield_requests` parameter that defaults to `False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: resolve_redirects declares `yield_requests: bool = False`.

items.claim: `CaseInsensitiveDict` is defined in `structures.py` and preserves the original case of keys while allowing case-insensitive lookups.
items.label: supported
items.reason: CaseInsensitiveDict is defined in structures.py, stores the original cased key alongside the value, and looks up by lowercased key.

items.claim: `CaseInsensitiveDict.items()` is inherited from `MutableMapping` and is driven by `__iter__` and `__getitem__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: CaseInsensitiveDict subclasses MutableMapping and defines only __iter__/__getitem__ etc., not items(), so items() comes from the ABC mixin.

items.claim: Session configuration merging is handled by `merge_setting` and `merge_hooks`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: merge_setting and merge_hooks are defined in sessions.py and used in prepare_request to merge session and request settings.

items.claim: `src/requests/__version__.py` defines `__author__` as "Kenneth Reitz".
items.label: supported
items.reason: __version__.py sets `__author__ = "Kenneth Reitz"`.

items.claim: `Response.is_redirect` returns `"location" in self.headers and self.status_code in REDIRECT_STATI`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: is_redirect returns `"location" in self.headers and self.status_code in REDIRECT_STATI`.

items.claim: `PreparedRequest.__init__` sets `method`, `url`, `headers`, `_cookies`, `body` and `_body_position` to `None`, and `hooks` to `{'response': []}`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: __init__ sets those attributes to None and hooks to default_hooks(), which is {'response': []}.

items.claim: `prepare_url` contains an early return: if `":" in url and not url.lower().startswith("http")`, it sets `self.url = url` and returns.
items.label: supported
items.reason: prepare_url returns early setting self.url = url for non-http schemes containing ':'.

items.claim: `requests.utils.select_proxy()` selects the appropriate proxy for a URL.
items.label: supported
items.reason: select_proxy in utils.py chooses a proxy for the given url from the proxies mapping.

items.claim: A password containing a character outside latin-1 causes `_basic_auth_str` to raise `UnicodeEncodeError` during preparation.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _basic_auth_str encodes a str password with latin1, which raises UnicodeEncodeError for characters outside latin-1, and it is invoked from prepare_auth.

items.claim: The pre-commit config includes `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` hooks.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The pre-commit config file contents were not shown.
